references.text: God tells Abraham that his wife Sarah will bear a son, and that he is to name him Isaac.
God sets the time for Isaac's birth – at the same time next year.
The Lord announces that Sarah will bear a son at the appointed time.
The Lord confirms that nothing is too hard for Him, and that Sarah will bear a son at the appointed time.
Paul points out that Abraham had two sons – one by the slave woman and one by the free woman – and that the son of the free woman was born through the promise.
Parallel structure in naming that highlights the contrast between Ishmael and Isaac.
New Testament interpretation of Isaac as 'only son' is based on his status as heir of the promise from the time of naming.
God's confirmation that the promise goes through Isaac, which forms the basis for the naming.
New Testament interpretation that illuminates the theological contrast between Ishmael and Isaac from the time of naming.
